title: Watching your vending machines
summary: Vending machines in Supermarket Simulator can be watched without walking to them: the game keeps a tracker for them, gives each machine a marker on the mini-map and holds what they contain in a list of its own.
body: A vending machine earns while you are somewhere else, so the game gives you a way to look at them remotely. There is a tracker for the machines and a tracker object behind it, which is why the shop's vending side can be read without walking the aisles.
Each machine has a marker of its own for the mini-map. That is how a machine can be shown where it stands rather than only being a line in a list.

What is inside a machine is kept as its own container, and the tracker reads from a list of its own. The stock a machine holds is therefore tracked as data about that machine rather than being counted off the front of the glass.

The tracker's panel is built to be used with a controller as well as with a mouse: there are handlers for the panel itself and for what it shows, so the same list can be scrolled and picked from with a pad.
Taking the money out is a state of its own. There is a collecting state, which is why emptying a machine is something the game can name rather than a transaction that leaves no trace.
The machine has a screen of its own with a tab, and that screen has a networked form, so looking at a machine in a shared shop reaches the same place as looking at one in a solo game.
Machines themselves have networked forms and a networked manager behind them, which is how a shared shop can keep several machines and their contents in step.
The two pictures beside this entry are the game's own: the vending machine itself, and the icon the game uses for the machine's computer screens.
What this entry does not tell you: how much a machine earns per sale, how many machines you may place, or how the tracker sorts them. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: A machine can be watched from elsewhere: there is a tracker and a tracker object for them.
Each machine has an object of its own for the mini-map.
What a machine holds is kept in a container, and the tracker's data has a list of its own.
The tracker panel is built for a controller, with handlers for the panel and for what it shows.
The machine's own screen has a tab, and there is a networked version of that tab.
Machines have networked forms and a networked manager behind them.
The game ships the machine's own picture and an icon for its computer screens.
Collecting from a machine is its own state.
A vending machine is marked on the map and in the world: a global map marker, a minimap marker and an icon of its own are named, with the machine's own screen and computer slot beside them.
facts.evidence: asset names: VendingGlobalMapMarker, VendingMachineMiniMapMarker, vendingMachineIcon, vendingMachineIconBG, VendingMachineScreen, Vending Computer Slot
